Hitchc.{{cite web |url=http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=44 |title=''Sphagneticola trilobata'' (herb) |work=Global Invasive Species Database |publisher=Invasive Species Specialist Group |date=2007-05-31 |access-date=2010-06-07 |archive-date=2011-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611180111/http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=44 |url-status=dead }} }} '''''Sphagneticola trilobata''''', commonly known as the '''Bay Biscayne creeping-oxeye''',{{PLANTS|id=SPTR6|taxon=Sphagneticola trilobata|access-date=25 November 2015}} '''marigold Singapore daisy''', '''creeping-oxeye''', '''trailing daisy,''' and '''wedelia''',{{Cite web |url=http://www.hear.org/pier/species/sphagneticola_trilobata.htm |title=Sphagneticola trilobata (PIER species info) |access-date=2013-02-25 |archive-date=2012-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121230065841/http://www.hear.org/Pier/species/Sphagneticola_trilobata.htm |url-status=dead }}{{ITIS |id=565537 |taxon=''Sphagneticola trilobata'' |access-date=2011-02-16}} is a plant in the tribe [[Heliantheae]] of the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to [[Mexico]], [[Central America]], and the [[Caribbean]], but now grows throughout the [[Neotropical realm|Neotropics]]. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental [[groundcover]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.iucngisd.org/gisd/species.php?sc=44|title=GISD|website=Iucngisd.org|access-date=28 March 2022}} ==Description== Spreading, [[groundcover|mat-forming]] perennial [[herb]] up to 30 cm in height. Has rounded stems up to 40 cm long, rooting at nodes and with the flowering stems ascending. Leaves are fleshy, hairy, 4–9 cm long and 2–5 cm wide, serrate or irregularly toothed, normally with pairs of lateral lobes, and dark green above and lighter green below. Its surface is hairy or glabrous, rarely scaly. ===Inflorescence=== [[Peduncle (botany)|Peduncle]]s are 3–10 cm long; involucres are campanulate to hemispherical, about 1 cm high; chaffy bracts are lanceolate, rigid. The flowers are bright yellow ray florets of about 8-13 per head, rays are 6–15 mm long; disk-corollas 4–5 mm long. The [[Pappus (botany)|pappus]] is a crown of short fimbriate scales. The seeds are tuberculate [[achenes]], 4–5 mm long. Propagation is mostly vegetatively as seeds are usually not fertile. In the tropics it is [[free-flowering]],[https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/3/3/3350 Sphagneticola trilobata (L.) Pruski] Flora Fauna Web. Retrieved 17 December 2023. and elsewhere it blooms mostly from spring to autumn.[https://www.daf.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0010/64000/singapore-daisy.pdf Singapore daisy Sphagneticola trilobata] The State of Queensland, ''[[Department of Agriculture and Fisheries]]'', 2023. Retrieved 17 December 2023. ==Habitat== It has a very wide [[ecological tolerance]] range, but grows best in sunny areas with well-drained, moist soil at low elevations.{{cite web|url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/?compid=5&dsid=56714&loadmodule=datasheet&page=481&site=144|title=Invasive Species Compendium|website=Cabi.org|access-date=28 March 2022}} ==Invasive species== ''Sphagneticola trilobata'' is listed in the IUCN's “[[List of the world's 100 worst invasive species]]”.{{cite web|url=https://www.iucngisd.org/gisd/pdf/100English.pdf|author1=Lowe S.|author2=Browne M.|author3=Boudjelas S.|author4=De Poorter M.|date=2000|title=100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species. A selection from the Global Invasive Species Database|publisher=The Invasive Species Specialist Group (ISSG)|access-date=28 March 2022}} It is [[Hemerochory|spread]] by people as an ornamental or groundcover that is planted in gardens, where it can [[garden escape|escape]] to surrounding areas by dumping of garden waste. It spreads vegetatively, not by seed. It rapidly forms a dense ground cover, crowding away and preventing other plant species from regenerating. This species is widely available as an ornamental and is therefore likely to spread further. It is a noxious weed in agricultural land, along roadsides urban waste places and other disturbed sites. It is also invasive along streams, canals, along the borders of mangrove swamps and in coastal vegetation. It is widespread as an [[invasive species]] on the [[Pacific Islands]], Hong Kong, South Africa, Australia, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka. {{Cite web |url=http://www.invasives.org.za/invasive-species/item/345-singapore-daisy-sphagneticola-trilobata.html |title=Singapore daisy | Sphagneticola trilobata - Invasives Species South Africa |access-date=2013-02-25 |archive-date=2014-09-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140907130946/http://www.invasives.org.za/invasive-species/item/345-singapore-daisy-sphagneticola-trilobata.html |url-status=dead }} ==Gallery== File:Sphagneticola trilobata in Singapore.jpg|Sphagneticola trilobata in [[Singapore]].
